correctness.rationale: For fixed m>=1, write a=rx, b=ry with gcd(x,y)=1 and x<y. Since gcd(x+y,xy)=1, a+b|mab iff x+y|mr, giving the exact sum E_m(X)=sum_(x<y,coprime) floor(X gcd(m,x+y)/(y(x+y))). A nonzero summand has y<sqrt(mX), so replacing floors has only O_m(X) total error. Möbius inversion converts the primitive condition into sum of reciprocal arithmetic progressions with inner sum log(2)/e+O(1/v) uniformly for e=d/gcd(d,r). Absolute convergence yields the logarithmic main term with A_d=1/zeta(2) product_(p^j||d)1/(p^(j-1)(p+1)); divisor expansion gcd(m,s)=sum_(d|m,d|s)phi(d) yields C_m=(3 log2/pi^2) product_(p^alpha||m)(1+alpha(p-1)/(p+1)). The m=1,2 constants have exact ratio 4/3. Independently enumerated direct ordered-positive pairs and coprime-parameter sum for m=1..5 and X=12,30,90; no inference to infinite asymptotic from experiments.

The m-local Euler product and O_m(X) remainder represent a genuinely structured all-fixed-m result, not just known-table recomputation.

limitations: m is fixed; O_m(X) not uniform in increasing m.
